videos.title: What next for the Democrats? | Martin Wolf on the US midterms | FT
videos.description:
Americans roundly rejected the Republican Party under President Donald Trump at the ballot box, giving the Democratic Party control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. 

That means Democrats have a raft of new tools with which to oppose Trump, including control of investigative committees the party may use to look into alleged corruption. How should the Democrats use that power? 

Does the scale of their victory mean they have the country’s backing, or just that Republicans were unpopular? And will Trump’s brand of politics return? Martin speaks to Nobel prize-winning economist Paul Krugman to discuss what happens next.

To enjoy future episodes, be sure to subscribe to ‘Martin Wolf on the World’ wherever you get your podcasts.

videos.title: How AI Is Changing Jobs in East Asia and Pacific | Regional Economic Update
videos.description:
How can artificial intelligence (AI) create better jobs, raise productivity, and increase incomes in East Asia and Pacific?

Watch the replay as World Bank economists Omar Arias and Patrick Kirby, co-authors of the October 2026 East Asia & Pacific Economic Update, explore how AI is changing jobs and skills across the region, how businesses can adopt AI, and what countries can do to ensure more workers benefit from a changing labor market.

The discussion explores:
- How businesses can adopt AI in ways that fit local needs
- How AI is changing the skills employers seek
- What policies can expand AI adoption and its economic benefits
Omar Arias and Patrick Kirby answered audience questions during the program, while Alessandro Barattieri, a co-author of the Economic Update, answered questions in the live chat.

Explore more resources and read the October 2026 East Asia & Pacific Economic Update: https://live.worldbank.org/en/event/2026/regional-economic-update-harnessing-ai-for-better-jobs-in-east-asia-and-pacific?cid=ECR_YT_worldbank_EN_EXT

videos.title: The Truth About How Data Centers Use Water And Power To Keep Cool
videos.description:
U.S. voters passed 40 ballot measures putting limits on AI data centers this week, as huge 1GW AI data centers from OpenAI, Meta, SpaceXAI, Amazon, Google and more push up water and power bills and put a strain on local resources. One of the issues that continues to come up is water usage, which is needed to cool the GPUs inside data centers running AI workloads. Closed-loop liquid cooling keeps water use low inside many modern AI data centers, but external cooling is still needed to move heat outside of the buildings and that requires large amounts of power or water in hot climates. CNBC visited data centers and spoke to researchers to find out the truth about how data centers use water.

videos.title: Ajay Banga on AI, Jobs & Opportunity | Global AI & Digital Summit
videos.description:
At the Global AI & Digital Summit in Seoul, World Bank Group President Ajay Banga discusses the future of development, the role of digital technology, and the opportunities and challenges presented by artificial intelligence.

He discusses the importance of getting the fundamentals of digital development right, including electricity, connectivity, affordability and digital public infrastructure, and shares examples of how locally relevant AI tools are being used in agriculture, health and education.

He also explores “small AI” and the opportunity for job creation and productivity through AI, particularly for developing countries, as well as the World Bank Group’s role in helping move promising solutions from pilots to delivery at scale.

Watch the conversation to hear his vision for using technology to drive jobs, productivity, dignity, and opportunity.
